# Additive tuning of 2026-10-24, skills round 1 confirmation, scenario 4

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:bc9ff145ae7bc2a53ece57ca1442ff3d5ef1528cca5641cbfc877419836a844a
lock: sha256:7b9b260a20cfe3c7b36337353499537aa39963f4be464ebcc9f28e55773eef36
selection: sha256:8d4747a05d1213146c97d37a574a457ce8aeee431a3f9f6a9c67c79021d1f437
read_set: sha256:f18e4fd7eafa09aabd6204d8a41112a4af8892eb03c0b5d7fb9d3bf5f927b3a3
seed: 0
harness: 0.6.1
tier: additive
arm: scenario-4
at: 2026-10-24
cost_cents: 10571
```

**This line is the confirmation of round 1 of the skills layer in the tuning round of the additive campaign, which [#1777](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1777) asked for.** The round screened four variants at 25 sessions each, and variant 1 ranked first, with the skills used in 23 of 25 sessions ([the screen of variant 1](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-24-skills-round-1-variant-1-scenario-4.md)). The confirmation runs that variant again at 145 sessions, against the best so far measured at the same count. Variant 1 makes `headwater-orient` the gate at the start of every task, and it adds to each skill a section that says how to run the engine, because the shipped skill bodies call `headwater`, which is not on the session's `PATH`. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-4 tuning`. It is the `scenario-4` arm of the additive tier over 5 probes of the tuning set, at 29 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `e303021c`, on the branch `tune/skills-r1-v1-pin`: `bea46653`, the variant's commit and the tool change of [#1857](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1857), which lets a pin be on a branch under `origin/tune/`. The pin was the same for the whole batch, and it is the commit the screen of variant 1 ran at. The canary of 8 sessions was read before `canary-passed` was written. The driver then halted five times from 46 of 145 sessions on the account's usage limit, and it continued in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 145 sessions and cost 10571 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 0 stopped at the turn cap, 0 stopped at the session budget, 105 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 4 passed 127 of 145 sessions, and 131 of 145 sessions used the skills layer. The keep row compares this line with the best so far of the layer, which passed 81 of 142 graded sessions and used the skills in 37 of 145 ([the best so far](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-24-skills-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-4.md)). The difference is +30.5 points, with the interval [+20.4, +39.9]. The whole interval is above zero, so the change is kept under the owner's rule of 2026-10-20 (#1777, ruling 7). The base row compares this line with the base of scenario 3, which passed 76 of 145 ([the base](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-24-base-re-measure-of-scenario-3.md)): +35.2 points, with the interval [+25.0, +44.4]. `try.sh result` closed round 1 of the skills layer as kept, and this line is now the layer's best so far.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,512.00 for the whole tuning round, over every attempt and every layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 12250 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 10782 cents against its cap, and the 145 recorded sessions account for 10571 cents of that sum. The 10782 cents go against the tuning ceiling of 129000 cents, which now holds 20940 cents.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1777/skills-r1-confirm/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.
